Fit a member of the Bregman-divergence framework, choosing the integration weight by cross-validation

cv.bregsurv.Rd

cv.bregsurv() is the package's main interface. It takes the three decisions the framework separates: the target model your data call for (target_cox(), target_ncc(), target_discrete(), linear or neural), the release the external source made (release_records(), release_coef(), release_score(), release_model()), and the member through which the release enters, which fixes the Bregman generator:

Usage

cv.bregsurv(
  target,
  release = NULL,
  member = NULL,
  penalty = c("none", "ridge", "lasso", "enet"),
  alpha = 0.5,
  etas = NULL,
  lambda = NULL,
  nlambda = 50,
  lambda.min.ratio = NULL,
  nfolds = 5,
  seed = 20260818L,
  criterion = NULL,
  standardize = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

target

A target from target_cox(), target_ncc() or target_discrete().

release

A release, or NULL for the target model alone.

member

"composite", "mahalanobis", "kl" or "none". NULL takes the first member the release supports: composite for records, Mahalanobis for coefficients with a precision matrix, Kullback-Leibler otherwise.

penalty

"none", "ridge", "lasso" or "enet" (elastic net with mixing alpha).

alpha

Elastic-net mixing parameter for penalty = "enet".

etas

Integration weights to search. NULL uses a log-spaced grid from 0.01 to the member's upper end, with 0 included.

lambda, nlambda, lambda.min.ratio

The penalty path; NULL builds a path for each eta.

nfolds

Number of folds.

seed

Seed of the fold assignment. The default is fixed, so repeated calls, and different members, share one partition.

criterion

Cross-validation criterion of the Cox ("V&VH", "LinPred", "CIndex_pooled", "CIndex_foldaverage") or matched ("loss", "AUC", "CIndex", "Brier") estimators. Members are comparable only under the same criterion; the discrete and neural targets use their own.

standardize

Standardize covariates for the penalized fits.

...

Further arguments passed to the underlying estimator.

Value

An object of class "cv.bregsurv" with the selected eta and lambda, the cross-validated value and its criterion, the coefficients of a linear target, the folds, the engine used and its full result in fit.

Details

  • "composite": the negative external log-likelihood, giving the composite likelihood (records);

  • "mahalanobis": a quadratic form, giving the Mahalanobis distance to the external coefficients (Euclidean when the release has no precision matrix);

  • "kl": the negative entropy on the model's conditional distributions (risk sets, or interval hazards for the discrete target), giving the Kullback-Leibler divergence;

  • "none": no release, the target model alone (the eta = 0 endpoint).

The integration weight eta (and, under a penalty, lambda) is chosen by nfolds-fold cross-validation on the target data. Every member fitted with the same seed on the same target is scored on the same partition by the same criterion, so their values can be compared directly: the cross-validated partial-likelihood loss of Verweij and Van Houwelingen for a Cox target, the conditional-likelihood loss for a matched design, and the held-out negative log-likelihood per subject for a discrete target.

Linear Cox and matched targets are fitted by the package's existing estimators (cv.coxkl, cv.cox_MDTL_enet, cv.ncc_indi, ...), named in the result's engine field; the result is identical to calling that estimator directly. The discrete-time target is fitted by Fisher scoring (proximal Newton under a lasso or elastic net), and neural targets by torch.

See also

bregsurv() for a fit at a given weight; targets, releases.

Examples

data(ExampleData_lowdim)
tr <- ExampleData_lowdim$train
tg <- target_cox(tr$time, tr$status, tr$z)
rl <- release_coef(ExampleData_lowdim$beta_external_fair)
kl  <- cv.bregsurv(tg, rl, member = "kl")
#> Warning: Stratum not provided. Treating all data as one stratum.
euc <- cv.bregsurv(tg, rl, member = "mahalanobis")
#> Warning: Stratum not provided. Treating all data as one stratum.
own <- cv.bregsurv(tg)                       # the target alone
#> Warning: Stratum not provided. Treating all data as one stratum.
c(kl = kl$value, euclidean = euc$value, target_only = own$value)
#>          kl   euclidean target_only 
#>    2.505875    2.511217    2.624735
